A1.justification: Both PDFs describe C-REX for referring expression counting, despite the changed title and substantial revision. Their complete text, equations, tables, figures, and supplementary materials are readable and support reliable comparison.

before.justification: V1 reports original C-REX and baseline experiments on REC-8K, FSC-147, and CARPK, including quantitative results, ablations, and qualitative examples.

after.justification: V2 reports original experiments across three architectures on REC-8K and FSC-147, plus contrastive-loss ablations, paraphrase robustness tests, and Molmo evaluation.

M1.justification: V1 selects positive tokens by cosine similarity to the class-masked referring expression, taking the top N tokens. V2 instead uses bipartite matching between predicted locations and ground-truth points, changing the contrastive labeling procedure and supervision. It also integrates C-REX into GroundingREC and CAD-GD by replacing their image-text losses while retaining their other objectives. The positive-anchor contrastive loss itself remains unchanged.

E1.justification: REC-8K and FSC-147 remain, but v2 removes the CARPK drone/parking-lot evaluation, eliminating v1's separate cross-dataset transfer test. V2 adds evaluation on paraphrased REC-8K expressions, introducing a linguistic-variation scenario.

E2.justification: V2 adds CAD-GD comparisons, including its density-guided inference variant, and Molmo2-4B. The FSC-147 comparison removes exemplar-based methods including FamNet, BMNet+, CounTR, and CACViT. Earlier REC comparators such as ZSC, TFOC, CounTX, and CountGD remain in supplementary Tables 6–7; their relocation is not removal.

E3.justification: Reported detection thresholds change from 0.30/0.36 to 0.25/0.35 for CLS/other tokens. V2 adds Swin-B configurations alongside Swin-T, reports precision and recall separately, evaluates density-guided CAD-GD inference, and specifies zero-shot and two-shot Molmo protocols. The count-range analysis also merges the three lowest bins into 0–20. These are substantive protocol changes, beyond newly disclosed training details.

E4.justification: V2 adds image-text versus image-only versus joint-loss ablations and paraphrase robustness testing. Its selection ablation adds bipartite matching and removes the N + 2log2(N) alternative. Count-range and qualitative analyses expand to paired comparisons across three architectures, while v1's attribute-wise MAE analysis and centroid-baseline component ablation disappear. The positive-anchor loss ablation is retained in Table 4b.

E5.justification: Neither version reports repeated-run counts, random seeds, confidence intervals, error bars, or significance tests. The sample counts accompanying count-range plots describe evaluation examples, not repeated runs.

E6.justification: V1's REC MAE/RMSE of 5.06/17.53 survives as the top-N ablation in v2 Table 4a. New matching-based GroundingDINO+C-REX results are 4.38/17.93 with Swin-T and 4.20/16.76 with Swin-B. V2 adds extensive architecture, paraphrase, and Molmo results while removing CARPK and attribute-level scores. Findings include CAD-GD paraphrase MAE worsening from 6.85 to 8.02 with C-REX. Changed methods and protocols preclude treating cross-version scores as same-setting gains.

T1.justification: The positive-set definition changes from the cosine-similarity arg-top-N construction in v1 Equations 2–3 to location-based bipartite matching in v2 Section 3. The supervised and modified contrastive-loss formulas otherwise remain algebraically unchanged. Neither version supplies formal theorems or proofs.

C1.justification: V1 presents identifying centroid prediction as a key counting component and constructing an improved baseline as central contributions. V2 drops that emphasis and foregrounds C-REX as a plug-in applicable to any REC architecture, demonstrated on three architectures. Its headline improvement claims change from over 22% MAE and 10% RMSE to up to 28% and 24.5% under the revised comparisons.

C2.justification: V2 introduces discussion of negative-token scarcity in extremely dense scenes and potential scaling with larger backbones. It interprets the joint-loss and Molmo experiments as support for specialized visual supervision, explicitly qualifies paraphrase robustness for CAD-GD, and illustrates accurate-looking counts that still select incorrect instances in Figure 8. V1's top-N label-noise justification and centroid-centered explanations are removed.

D1.justification: V2 newly documents 20/30-epoch training schedules, learning-rate decay, checkpoint/retraining provenance, and CAD-GD density-map construction. It omits v1's explicit AdamW optimizer, weight decay of 1e-4, and loss weights of 1, 5, and 0.005. The direct code-repository link becomes a project-page link. These are documentation and access-instruction changes; the PDFs do not establish changes to omitted parameters or actual resource availability.

R1.justification: V2 substantially expands research positioning: CAD-GD becomes an important REC predecessor, counting VQA is distinguished from localized REC, intra-image contrastive learning is related to person re-identification, and VLM/tool-based counting is discussed. These additions introduce substantive comparisons and citations beyond v1's focus on GroundingREC and detection-versus-density counting.

P1.justification: The title, abstract, introduction, and conclusion are extensively rewritten around embedding-space choice and architectural portability. The baseline-centered method subsection disappears, remaining method explanations are reordered and expanded, and the supplementary narrative is reorganized. This is substantial editorial restructuring beyond adding experiments.

P2.justification: The document changes from two-column to single-column layout. The original pipeline figure is replaced by two conceptual comparisons, tables are rebuilt around paired baseline/C-REX configurations and backbones, and qualitative grids are extensively revised. The earlier REC comparison is split and moved to supplementary tables; the count-range plot is regrouped and the attribute-wise chart removed.

improvement.justification: V2 substantially strengthens evidence for the central embedding-space and portability claims through three-architecture comparisons and direct image-text/image-only/joint-loss ablations, addressing important gaps in v1. Paraphrase and expanded failure analyses also clarify applicability. These gains outweigh the removed CARPK and attribute analyses and reduced hyperparameter disclosure. Some conclusions still overgeneralize: Table 4a shows worse test RMSE for matching than top-N selection, and Table 2 shows GroundingREC test MAE worsening from 10.12 to 12.46 with C-REX.
